# Bounded-state scorecard v0 -- generated, do not hand-edit
seed=20261123 python=3.11.2

## A. The two walls

A1. Pigeonhole. A state of W bits has 2^W values; more than 2^W distinct histories must
    collide, and colliding histories exist that need different answers. Bounded state =>
    lossless unbounded recall is impossible. No design escapes this.

| W (bits) | states 2^W | tokens until collision floor at 1 bit/token |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 6.554e+04 | 65,536 |
| 24 | 1.678e+07 | 16,777,216 |
| 32 | 4.295e+09 | 4,294,967,296 |
| 40 | 1.100e+12 | 1,099,511,627,776 |
| 48 | 2.815e+14 | 281,474,976,710,656 |
| 64 | 1.845e+19 | 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 |

A2. Energy. q independent queries over an answer set of size S need >= q*log2(S) bits
    of *somewhere* -- working RAM, or an addressable store.

| queries q | answer set S | bits required | KiB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+04 | 1.905e+00 |
| 100,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+06 | 1.905e+02 |
| 1,000,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+07 | 1.905e+03 |

    Read together: RAM must stay O(1) (R2), so the bits live in the store, so the only
    honest claim is *constant working state*, and the measured question becomes cost per
    generated token (G4). A primitive whose per-token reads grow is attention renamed.

## B. Dense associative memory: exactness vs load factor

dim D=128, keys/values in {-1,+1}, closed-form outer-product training, 7 seeds,
recall = fraction of stored patterns returned bit-exactly; false = fraction of random
unseen keys answered with confidence > 0.5 (interference, the thing exactness forbids).

| load N/D | N | exact recall | false answers | state bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.125 | 16 | 81.2% | 0.0% | 64 KiB |
| 0.250 | 32 | 17.9% | 0.0% | 64 KiB |
| 0.375 | 48 | 0.3% | 8.3% | 64 KiB |
| 0.500 | 64 | 0.0% | 34.2% | 64 KiB |
| 0.750 | 96 | 0.0% | 85.0% | 64 KiB |
| 1.000 | 128 | 0.0% | 98.3% | 64 KiB |

    Reading: exactness is 100% only far below capacity, then falls off a cliff --
    interference is not a tuning problem, it is the pigeonhole wall of A1 wearing a
    matrix. *Closed-form training is not the bottleneck*; the collapsed representation is.

## C. KV-cache accounting (the baseline the primitive must beat)

fp16, D=2048, L=32 layers. bytes(state) and bytes *read per generated token*.

| n (tokens) | KV state | G2 ratio (state) | read / token | G4 (<=4 KiB) | G3 proxy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 250.00 MiB | 1.0x | 250.00 MiB | FAIL | 1.0x |
| 10,000 | 2500.00 MiB | 10.0x | 2500.00 MiB | FAIL | 10.0x |
| 100,000 | 25000.00 MiB | 100.0x | 25000.00 MiB | FAIL | 100.0x |
| 1,000,000 | 250000.00 MiB | 1000.0x | 250000.00 MiB | FAIL | 1000.0x |

    G2 fails (state grows linearly), G3 fails (per-token cost grows linearly),
    G4 fails by ~10^4. A candidate that 'compresses the cache' keeps every one of
    these curves; only O(1) reads/token changes the last two columns.

## D. Composition: trainer or representation?  (K3 preview)

Task y=(a+b) mod 10. Seen: a,b < 7. Held out: any pair with a or b >= 7.
Seen pairs are the only thing any trainer sees.

| model | trainer | params | train s | seen acc | held-out acc | gap (G6 <= 5 pts) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joint one-hot, linear | closed form (ridge) | 101*10 | 0.01 | 100.0% | 5.9% | 94.1 |
| pair one-hot, bilinear | closed form (counts) | 1000 | 0.000 | 100.0% | 11.8% | 88.2 |
| joint one-hot, MLP-64 | SGD/backprop | 7040 | 1.88 | 100.0% | 5.9% | 94.1 |

    PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (written before this script ran): D2 'generalises
    perfectly because its table is of the operation, not of the data'.
    MEASURED: D2 held-out = 11.8%. The prediction is FALSIFIED and stays on the record.
    Why: T[a][b] is indexed by *concrete operands*, so an unseen operand pair addresses
    a row that was never written. A table of data is a table of data whatever shape
    it has. All three models are lookup tables of the pairs; all three fail the same way.
    * D1 and D3 share a representation and both score identically -- 3000 steps of
      backprop bought exactly what the features already gave. Trainer is not the axis.
    * So the axis is: does the *same* parameter block get reused across different
      operands and positions? Report D4 tests that, and D4 was added AFTER seeing D2
      fail, so it is labelled [post-hoc] and cannot become the load-bearing term (NC-4).

## D4 [post-hoc]. Does sharing the operation table across positions buy composition?

y=(a+b) mod 100. One shared table over (digit_a, digit_b, carry), applied recursively
over 2 positions. Train only on a,b < 16 (256 pairs).

| model | table entries | seen acc | held-out correct | **held-out WRONG** | abstain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shared table, recursive | 104 | 100.0% | 55.7% | **0** / 9744 | 44.3% |

    Precision on everything it answers: 100.0%. It never guessed wrong.
    Compare D2 (one table per operand pair, 10000 rows, unshared): held-out 11.8%,
    and every unseen row is a confident wrong answer. Same closed-form trainer, same task,
    10000 rows -> 104 rows, and the failure mode changed from *silent wrong* to
    *locally-attributable abstention*.

    So the axis is not trainer, capacity, or regularisation: it is **parameter sharing
    across positions/roles**, which also makes the model's incompetence *enumerable*.
    A three-way outcome (correct / wrong / abstain-with-cause) is a capability a softmax
    Transformer cannot express at all, and it is measurable. Adopt it as G8 (see charter).

---- total wall clock 11.1s on CPU ----

## VERDICT ON THREAD 0002's K3 CONTROL

**0.1% was a defect in the measuring instrument, not a fact about the task and not a
finding about difficulty.** Three concrete defects (BUG-1, BUG-2, BUG-3), each of which
alone is enough to make every method look dead. None of them is fixed by tuning a model.

* The task IS learnable. IN-SPLIT, with all digit values observed and only pairs held
  out, the counted role table reaches 100.00% exact and backprop-one-hot reaches
  29.2% exact (96.9% on the units digit alone).
  "The task was too small for anyone" is therefore false as stated.
* 0.1% is exactly 1/1000 -- chance. On a population whose symbols never appeared in
  training, chance is the only available score for a symbol-blind learner, so the
  number carries no information about task size, model quality, or the primitive.
* What the corrected harness DOES find is a real difference, and it is not accuracy:
  under an unseen-symbol split the counted table answers NOTHING WRONG (it abstains),
  while backprop-one-hot is confidently wrong on essentially every scored item. That is
  G8 -- calibrated abstention -- measured against a same-data, larger-parameter baseline
  for the first time. Coverage and precision must be read separately; a table that
  abstains is not beaten by a model that guesses.

For the record: every claim in thread 0002 that rests on the BP control -- including
"nobody learns the task" and "the task was too small for any of the four systems" --
is withdrawn as unsupported. The 4.4% / 2555-wrong closed-form numbers are unaffected:
they are counts, they reproduce exactly, and they remain the valid part of that thread.

## Part 3. Audit of every number in this file

**Conditions.** Intel Xeon @ 2.60 GHz, 2 vCPU, Linux 6.1, python 3.11.2 (GCC 12.2.0), CPU-only,
stdlib only, no GPU anywhere in the loop. Every script run twice from a clean checkout in separate
processes; "deterministic" below means stdout was identical after masking timing fields.

| script | seed | run 1 | run 2 | two runs identical | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scorecard.py` | 20261123 | 10.7 s | 10.5 s | yes, except the wall-clock line and one `train s` cell | **certified** |
| `symmetry.py` | none used | 0.06 s | 0.06 s | yes, byte-identical | **certified** |
| `carry.py` | none used (fixed init) | 14.2 s | 14.3 s | yes, byte-identical | counts certified; **conclusion withdrawn**, see C1 |
| `k3control.py` (new) | 20261123 | 179.9 s | 180.2 s | yes, except timing | **certified** |

`certify.py --full` re-ran all four twice from scratch: **12/12 checks pass** in 436 s. That run re-measured `k3control.py` at 182.2 s / 181.4 s under load -- timing is the only field that moves, which is the point of masking exactly it.

Nothing in Part 1 is unseeded, and nothing in Part 1 depends on the machine: the only
machine-dependent output is wall clock. The problems below are not determinism problems; they are
*comparability* problems, which are worse.

### Confirmed

Every model number in §A–§D and §D4 reproduces on both runs, to the digit. The pigeonhole and
energy arithmetic (§A) and the KV accounting (§C) are closed-form and machine-independent. §D4's
55.7% / 0 wrong / 44.3% abstain reproduces exactly. thread 0001's kill reproduces exactly.

### Corrected or challenged -- each with the measurement that forces it

1. **`carry.py`'s K3 control is invalid, and so is every conclusion drawn from it.** Two defects:
   its input vector has `BASE*BASE = 100` features built from positions 0 and 1 only, so *position 2
   of both operands never reaches the model* and the scored 3-digit target is unidentifiable by
   construction; and its 0.1% is measured on `held[::397] = 2,519` pairs while the closed-form
   numbers beside it are measured on 999,964. `certify.py` checks C1-C3 assert both.
   **0.1% is also exactly 1/1000 -- chance.** A number equal to chance, on a population whose
   symbols were never observed, is not evidence about task size. It was reported as evidence.
   Consequence: "nobody learns the task" and "the task was too small for any of the four systems"
   are **withdrawn as unsupported**. See Part 2 for what replaces them. (Its docstring also claims
   `< 10 s`; measured 14.2 s. Small, and the same species of error: a written claim nobody ran.)

2. **§B's headline sentence is not measured by §B's table.** It says exactness "is 100% only far
   below capacity". The lowest load tested is N/D = 0.125, where recall is **81.2%**. No row in the
   table reaches 100%, so the location of the 100% threshold is unknown. Fix: sweep N/D down to
   ~0.01, or delete the sentence. (`certify.py` C5.)

3. **§B's "confidence > 0.5" is not a confidence.** The criterion is `abs(y_i) > 0.5*dim` on an
   unnormalised inner product whose magnitude grows with N and dim. It is a magnitude threshold
   whose meaning changes with the load factor, so the "false answers" column is not comparable
   across rows. The qualitative reading (interference rises with load to 98.3%) survives; the
   column's label does not.

4. **§D4 was published without a same-size baseline**, which the team's own hard rule forbids:
   D4's 104 entries were compared against D2's 10,000 rows, a 96x difference in stored entries.
   A same-budget, no-sharing table is now measured in Part 2 §R1: **200 entries shared -> 100.00%
   exact; 200 entries unshared -> 0.00% exact, 100% abstain.** At equal capacity the sharing claim
   survives. It had not been tested at equal capacity before.

5. **§D4's mechanism is a mixture, and the mixture was not disclosed.** `predict()` indexes the
   table by carry *and* recomputes carry arithmetically (`c = 1 if (x + y + c) >= base else 0`).
   So "parameter sharing across positions is the axis" names one of two mechanisms. Thread 0002's
   own V1 result -- removing the carry *index* turns abstention into 2,555 confident errors --
   shows the computed-carry term is load-bearing. D4 must be re-labelled as *sharing + computed
   carry*, and the NC-1 ablation of each term is still missing. (`certify.py` C4.)

6. **0001's cause was asserted, not measured; now measured.** The post-mortem says the missing cell
   set "is closed under transposition". `symmetry.py` measures the gain (0.0 pts) but never checks
   closure. Checked: **96 of 96** missing `(x,y,c)` cells have a missing mirror, so folding a
   verified symmetry could rescue exactly 0. The stated cause is correct -- and the script should
   have printed the check, because a kill with the right number and the wrong reason is a trap for
   the next candidate. (`certify.py` C6.)

7. **"A softmax Transformer cannot express abstention at all" is asserted, not measured.** A model
   with an explicit abstain class or a threshold can emit one. What is unmeasured is whether the
   abstention is *calibrated*. This is the claim G8 actually needs, and it needs a baseline run.

8. **The Builder's own bug, kept on the record.** The first version of `k3control.py` selected its
   train/test split with a linear hash of `(a, b)`. Any linear hash preserves the parity of `a+b`:
   it trained only on even sums and scored only on odd ones, so every backprop model returned
   exactly 0.0% on the units digit -- the very failure being audited, reproduced inside the
   instrument. Fixed with `splitmix64`, and the failed pre-registration (P1-P4) is kept in Part 2.
   This is why the audit rule is "two independent runs", not "one careful run".

### What the audit changes

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| "Every method failed; the task was too small for anyone" | The instrument failed. On a fair split the counted table is exact (100.00%) and backprop reaches 29.21% exact / 96.9% units. |
| "Closed-form training is not the bottleneck" (§B prose) | True for §D1 vs §D3 (identical representation, identical score). Not established for §B, where the claim about 100% has no row behind it. |
| "Parameter sharing is the axis" (§D4) | Survives at equal capacity (100.00% vs 0.00%), but carries an unablated second mechanism: computed carry. |
| "Abstention is a capability" | Now measured against a same-data, larger-parameter baseline: 0 wrong vs 6,481-7,956 wrong. See Part 2 §R2. |

### Known gaps in this audit

- `k3control.py` gives the backprop baseline 2,000 training pairs and 60 epochs; the counted table
  uses the same 2,000. Whether backprop would close the gap with 100x more pairs is untested here
  and is a legitimate attack on P6.
- The backprop baseline's output factorisation (3 x 10 heads) is a representation choice I made for
  runtime; it is disclosed in the source, and it is applied to both encodings, but it means this is
  not a "same-size Transformer" -- it is a small MLP. No Transformer baseline has been run on CPU.
- The convergence checkpoints in Part 2 are scored on the first 1,000 probe pairs, while the final
  figure is scored on all 8,000 -- so `ep60: 26.8%` and the headline `29.21%` are the same model on
  two different probe slices, not a contradiction. It reads like one unless this line is here.
- G1-G8 are still only partly measurable. G3/G4 have never been measured on a *candidate*; only on
  the KV accounting of a hypothetical baseline.
